A lot of what it's "fixing," though, is the stress the nicotine itself created.

That doesn't mean your stress wasn't real or that you have to decide to quit right now. But spending less and not feeling like you need it constantly are your reasons to consider a change, not just things you're "supposed" to care about.
When you use regularly, going without it can bring on tension or irritability, so a hit can feel like it's fixing stress while also keeping that cycle going.
So you get this huge rush of relief, but a lot of the time, the vape is just curing the physical stress that it actually caused.
Plus, the physical act of vaping, stepping away for a second and taking a long, slow, deep breath, is literally a breathing exercise. It forces your nervous system to chill out for a minute.
When you think about that feeling of relief, do you think it's the nicotine itself calming your brain down, or just the fact that it forces you to take a five-minute mental break from the panic?
